examples.label: Confirm AJP/8009 and HTTP/8080 are open
Read WEB-INF/web.xml through the Ghostcat (CVE-2020-1938) LFI

notes: CVE-2020-1938 reads (and sometimes includes) files under the app root via AJP/8009 with no credentials - ideal for pulling WEB-INF/web.xml and leaked manager creds.

recommended.note: Use creds leaked from config files to hit the manager.

name: Tomcat - Ghostcat AJP LFI (CVE-2020-1938)
description: Ghostcat abuses the AJP connector (port 8009) to read files inside the web app, disclosing WEB-INF/web.xml and other sensitive files; can lead to RCE if uploads are possible.

defense.why_it_works: Ghostcat (CVE-2020-1938) exploits a flaw in Tomcat's AJP connector. AJP attribute injection allows an unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary files from any deployed webapp, including WEB-INF/web.xml which may contain credentials.
defense.prerequisites: AJP connector exposed on port 8009 (default in Tomcat < 9.0.31). Network access to port 8009.
defense.impact: Read any webapp file: WEB-INF/web.xml (credentials), application.properties, log files. If file upload is possible, can achieve RCE by including an uploaded file as JSP.
defense.detection: Unexpected connection to port 8009 from non-localhost IP. AJP protocol traffic in network capture. tomcat-ajp.lfi.py signature in access logs.
defense.artifacts: Network flow to port 8009 from external IP | Tomcat access log (AJP requests) | IDS alert for AJP-based LFI pattern
defense.prevention: Upgrade Tomcat to 9.0.31+, 8.5.51+, or 7.0.100+. If AJP not needed, disable the connector. If needed, set secret attribute and bind to localhost only.
defense.misconfiguration: AJP connector enabled on 0.0.0.0:8009 in server.xml without secret attribute and without firewall restriction.
defense.vulnerable_config:
<!-- server.xml default -->
<Connector port="8009" protocol="AJP/1.3"
           redirectPort="8443"/>  <!-- no secret, no address restriction -->
defense.secure_config:
<!-- Option 1: disable AJP -->
<!-- Remove or comment out the AJP Connector -->

<!-- Option 2: secure AJP -->
<Connector protocol="AJP/1.3"
           address="127.0.0.1"
           port="8009"
           redirectPort="8443"
           secret="strong-random-secret"/>
defense.evasion: Port 8009 often not checked by default egress firewall rules.
